question: What is the main purpose of a problem statement in a research proposal?

options.A: Convinces the reader that a specific issue requires study
options.B: Lists the exact financial cost of the research project
options.C: Provides a complete list of all hospital staff members
options.D: Summarizes the final results found after data collection

explanation: A problem statement points out the exact gap or trouble in current clinical practice that your research is going to help fix. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h4)

question: What condition often develops if Wernicke encephalopathy is left untreated?

options.A: Rheumatoid arthritis
options.B: Chronic kidney failure
options.C: Type 2 diabetes
options.D: Korsakoff syndrome

explanation: That's correct! If Wernicke's isn't caught and treated, it often rolls into Korsakoff syndrome, which brings long-term memory troubles. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical hurdle when trying to use healthcare audit recommendations?

options.A: Severe budget constraints limiting new purchases
options.B: Lack of strong backing from hospital executive leadership
options.C: Instant and enthusiastic compliance from all veteran staff members
options.D: Resistance to change from employees used to old routines

explanation: Change is tough! People rarely jump up to follow new rules instantly without some resistance. Overcoming old habits is one of the biggest challenges leaders face. [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h7)

question: Why does the internal urethral sphincter need to close tightly during emission?

options.A: To slow down the heart rate during arousal
options.B: To allow urine to mix freely with seminal fluid
options.C: To increase testosterone production in the testes
options.D: To prevent retrograde movement of semen into the bladder

explanation: Exactly! Closing that door ensures semen goes forward out of the penis instead of taking a wrong turn backward into the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T5#GNS121_U4_T5_h3)

question: What does a high D-dimer blood test result usually tell you?

options.A: A complete absence of circulating platelets
options.B: An immediate dietary need for vitamin K supplementation
options.C: The rapid breakdown of unwanted blood clots in the body
options.D: An inherited deficiency in factor VIII production

explanation: D-dimer is like a leftover wrapper from a dissolved clot! If it's high, it means clots are actively forming and breaking down somewhere in the body, such as in DVT or DIC. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h6)

question: Where should you place your hands when giving abdominal thrusts to a conscious adult who is choking?

options.A: Across the soft throat area
options.B: Just above the navel
options.C: In the center of the chest
options.D: Directly over the lower ribs

explanation: Correct! Placing your fist just above the belly button (and well below the ribs) lets you push the diaphragm up safely without breaking any bones. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h5)

question: How does population diversity affect the sample size you need for a study?

options.A: Diversity has no impact on the required number of participants
options.B: A more diverse population requires a smaller sample size
options.C: Diverse populations can only be studied using convenience sampling
options.D: A more diverse population requires a larger sample size

explanation: You got it! If the group has many different backgrounds and experiences, you need a bigger sample to capture all those variations accurately. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h5)

question: You notice that the sharps box in the treatment room is filled right past the max line. What should you do?

options.A: Transfer some of the used needles into a regular plastic trash bin
options.B: Push the protruding syringes down firmly with a gloved hand to create more room
options.C: Close and seal the container safely for disposal, then replace it with a new one
options.D: Leave the container open until the end of the week to save on plastic bags

explanation: Never push down on a full sharps box! Once it reaches the fill line, lock it up safely, throw it out according to protocol, and grab a fresh one. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T4#GNS122_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary characteristic of a malignant neoplasm compared to a benign one?

options.A: It invades nearby tissues and spreads to other parts of the body.
options.B: It stops growing entirely after a few weeks without treatment.
options.C: It only affects older adults and ignores younger populations.
options.D: It stays localized in one spot and never grows very large.

explanation: Malignant neoplasms are cancerous because they can break away, invade surrounding structures, and travel through the blood or lymph system. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T12#GNS321_U1_T12_h1)

question: Which of these options is NOT something a nurse needs to track after giving an antidote?

options.A: Daily shoe size and foot width measurements
options.B: Continuous vital signs and breathing patterns
options.C: Relevant laboratory markers and blood gas results
options.D: Neurological alertness and mental status

explanation: Your patient's shoe size won't tell you how they are recovering from poison! Breathing, alertness, and lab results are what truly matter. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h6)

question: How often should breaths be delivered once an advanced airway is in place during adult cardiac arrest?

options.A: Every 30 seconds
options.B: Every 6 seconds
options.C: Every 2 seconds
options.D: Every 15 seconds

explanation: Giving one breath every 6 seconds equals about 10 breaths per minute, which is the safe target rate. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h4)

question: Who serves as the vital link between frontline nursing care and software developers?

options.A: Pharmacy technicians
options.B: Hospital billing clerks
options.C: Nurse informaticians
options.D: Biomedical electricians

explanation: Exactly right! Nurse informaticians combine real bedside nursing experience with computer science to help design better healthcare tech. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h7)

question: In a SMART aim, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Mandatory
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Manual
options.D: Maximum

explanation: In the SMART goal framework, 'M' stands for measurable. It means your goal must include clear numbers or signs so you know if you are actually making progress. [learn more](GST319_U3_T3#GST319_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the general long-term outlook for a patient who has a benign heart tumour completely removed?

options.A: Poor, with a life expectancy of only a few weeks
options.B: Hopeless without a full heart transplant
options.C: Guarded, because benign tumours always spread to the liver
options.D: Excellent, with most patients returning to normal activities

explanation: Once a benign tumour is successfully taken out, the cure rate is super high and patients usually get right back to their normal lives. Wonderful news for patients! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T8#GNS213_U1_T8_h8)

question: Which class of blood pressure medication works primarily by helping the kidneys remove excess water and sodium from the body?

options.A: Diuretics
options.B: Statins
options.C: Antibiotics
options.D: Beta-blockers

explanation: Diuretics, or water pills, prompt the kidneys to excrete sodium and water, reducing overall blood volume and pressure. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T16#GNS324_U4_T16_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of placing electrode pads on a patient's chest for cardiac monitoring?

options.A: To capture the electrical activity and heart rhythm
options.B: To measure the exact temperature of the heart muscle
options.C: To keep the patient warm during cold hospital nights
options.D: To deliver mild electric shocks to warm the skin

explanation: Electrodes pick up the heart's electrical impulses and display them as a waveform on the screen. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T2#GNS113_U4_T2_h3)

question: Who can show leadership in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Only the appointed director of nursing
options.B: Only nurses with over twenty years of experience
options.C: Any nurse guiding care and supervising colleagues
options.D: Hospital chief executive officers exclusively

explanation: You don't need a fancy title to be a leader! Leadership is about your actions and positive influence. Even as a junior or staff nurse, you lead every time you guide patient care or help a colleague. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is a literature review so important when writing a proposal?

options.A: To criticize every nurse who worked before you
options.B: To fill up empty pages in the research document
options.C: To identify existing knowledge gaps on the topic
options.D: To gather personal opinions from hospital patients

explanation: Reviewing past studies shows you what has already been done and helps you find out what is still missing so your study adds real value. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why can damage to the pons mess up normal sleep patterns?

options.A: It monitors blood oxygen levels specifically while sleeping.
options.B: It houses neural circuits that regulate REM sleep and muscle relaxation.
options.C: It directly generates conscious awareness during the night.
options.D: It controls the production of melatonin in the pineal gland.

explanation: Pontine structures play a big role in dreaming (REM sleep) and making sure our muscles stay relaxed so we don't act out our dreams. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h3)

question: What kind of information does qualitative research usually collect?

options.A: Machine-recorded heart monitor printouts
options.B: Exact laboratory blood test numbers
options.C: Statistical charts of hospital bed capacity
options.D: Words, interviews, and personal experiences

explanation: Spot on! Qualitative research explores human feelings and experiences by collecting descriptive text through interviews and observation. Think 'qual' for quality and stories! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which method helps reduce participant dropout in a long-term study?

options.A: Keeping updated contact information and building good rapport
options.B: Making the questionnaires as long and complex as possible
options.C: Changing the research topic completely every six months
options.D: Refusing to communicate with participants between visits

explanation: Great choice! Staying in touch, being friendly, and treating participants with respect makes them want to stick with the study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T11#GNS224_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest number of calories per gram?

options.A: Fat
options.B: Protein
options.C: Water
options.D: Carbohydrate

explanation: Fats are the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying nine kilocalories for every single gram consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: A medication needs to pass into the interior of a cell. Which structure must it cross first?

options.A: Golgi apparatus
options.B: Plasma membrane
options.C: Nuclear envelope
options.D: Endoplasmic reticulum

explanation: The plasma membrane forms the outer boundary of the cell, so any substance entering from the outside environment must cross it first. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T5#GNS111_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of health care financing in a population?

options.A: Mobilizing, pooling, and allocating funds for health services
options.B: Generating high profits for pharmaceutical companies
options.C: Eliminating private hospitals from the healthcare market
options.D: Reducing the number of nursing training institutions

explanation: Health financing is fundamentally about gathering and distributing money to pay for needed health services. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why is communication considered a two-way process in the IEC framework?

options.A: It focuses only on passing medical news from the hospital to the village
options.B: It requires two different nurses to speak at the same community meeting
options.C: It means printing health materials in both English and a local language
options.D: It involves listening to community feedback and addressing local fears

explanation: Effective communication in IEC goes beyond just giving orders; it requires listening to what the community has to say and clearing up doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to know the virulence of a germ?

options.A: It shows how quickly the hospital laboratory can bill the patient.
options.B: It helps predict how severe the tissue damage and symptoms might be.
options.C: It dictates the patient's visiting hours in the hospital ward.
options.D: It determines the exact room temperature the patient needs.

explanation: Virulence tells us how strong or nasty a germ is. Knowing this helps you anticipate how sick your patient could get so you can plan better care. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why does eating a fatty meal trigger severe pain in someone with gallstones?

options.A: Stomach acid mixes with fat to create a toxic gas.
options.B: The liver swells instantly from eating too much oil.
options.C: The gallbladder contracts to release bile against blocked stones.
options.D: Fat directly irritates the lining of the stomach.

explanation: When fat hits the small intestine, your gallbladder squeezes to send out bile. If gallstones are blocking the path, that squeeze causes sharp pain! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h4)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of severe diabetic ketoacidosis?

options.A: Excessive hair growth
options.B: Slow and deep sleep
options.C: Fruity breath odor
options.D: Yellowing of the skin

explanation: When ketones build up in dangerous amounts, they give the patient's breath a distinct, sweet, fruity scent. Good clinical clue! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h8)

question: What is an important goal when assessing a patient with neurasthenia?

options.A: Encouraging them to ignore all physical sensations
options.B: Proving to them that their symptoms are entirely imagined
options.C: Validating their experience of pain and building trust
options.D: Rushing through the interview to save hospital time

explanation: You're a natural! Patients often feel brushed off when lab tests come back normal. Believing their pain builds the trust they need to heal. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h4)

question: Which type of bacterial toxin is released only when the bacterial cell wall breaks apart?

options.A: Exotoxins
options.B: Coagulase
options.C: Endotoxins
options.D: Antitoxins

explanation: Endotoxins stay tucked inside the outer wall of certain bacteria (Gram-negative) and are only set free when the bacteria break down. [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is a major duty of a nurse working in a hospital ward?

options.A: Living with families to supervise their daily meal preparation
options.B: Building local community infrastructure and public roads
options.C: Acting as a direct caregiver and monitor of acute treatments
options.D: Operating primary health clinics without physician oversight

explanation: Right on! Hospital nurses spend their shifts giving hands-on care, giving meds, and keeping a close eye on acutely ill patients. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T3#GNS112_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the main job of an umbilical cord clamp?

options.A: To hold the sewing needle steady during repairs
options.B: To safely stop blood flow through the cut cord stump
options.C: To gently clear mucus from the newborn's nose
options.D: To clamp blood vessels inside the mother's uterus

explanation: Cord clamps lock tightly onto the baby's cord right after it's cut to keep the baby safe from any bleeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is it wonderful to let a patient pick out their own clothes for the day?

options.A: It saves time during morning care
options.B: It matches hospital uniform rules
options.C: It builds personal dignity and self-esteem
options.D: It keeps the clothes clean longer

explanation: Spot on! Small choices like picking an outfit give patients back control and boost their mood all day long. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T2#GNS324_U6_T2_h5)

question: What happens when stool enters the rectum and you decide to hold it in for a bit?

options.A: The gut nerves completely reverse the direction of the waste.
options.B: The voluntary outer muscle contracts to override the reflex.
options.C: The parasympathetic nerves shut down all feeling completely.
options.D: The involuntary inner valve tightens up even more.

explanation: You consciously squeeze your skeletal external sphincter to keep things in check when it's not the right time or place to use the restroom. Perfectly normal! [learn more](GNS121_U1_T13#GNS121_U1_T13_h3)

question: How does fee-for-service differ fundamentally from capitation?

options.A: Providers are paid based on each specific test or treatment performed
options.B: Patients pay the doctor directly with farm produce
options.C: The hospital receives the exact same amount every month forever
options.D: No money changes hands until the end of the calendar year

explanation: Under fee-for-service, payment is tied directly to the volume of services rendered rather than a fixed advance sum per patient. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main idea behind convenience sampling?

options.A: Using a computer program to select names randomly
options.B: Asking participants to refer other qualified friends
options.C: Dividing the population into equal demographic groups
options.D: Choosing participants who are easiest to reach and recruit

explanation: You nailed it! Convenience sampling is all about grabbing whoever is readily available—like the students sitting right next to you in class. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h4)

question: Why would a nurse researcher choose a cross-sectional design?

options.A: To find out how many people currently have a specific health issue
options.B: To test the long-term effects of a new surgical procedure
options.C: To track how a chronic illness changes in a patient from childhood to old age
options.D: To prove that one specific drug directly cures a disease over time

explanation: This design is your go-to when you want a quick snapshot of how common a health issue is right now in your community. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h1)

question: What is the most trusted and widely used method of sterilization in the TSSU?

options.A: Boiling in water for ten minutes
options.B: Washing with strong liquid bleach
options.C: Ultraviolet light exposure cabinets
options.D: Steam under pressure in an autoclave

explanation: You're doing great! The autoclave is the gold standard because hot steam under pressure quickly destroys all germs and tough spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: Why do hospitals prefer phased construction plans over shutting down completely during expansions?

options.A: They allow construction workers to finish the project in one day
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for architectural blueprints
options.C: They prevent the hospital from ever needing future maintenance
options.D: They minimize disruption to ongoing patient care services

explanation: Building section by section allows the hospital to keep its doors open, caring for patients safely while construction happens away from active wards. [learn more](GST321_U4_T5#GST321_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which home health team member specializes in treating swallowing disorders and speech difficulties?

options.A: Speech-language pathologist
options.B: Physical therapist
options.C: Occupational therapist
options.D: Licensed practical nurse

explanation: Speech therapists assess and treat patients who have trouble speaking, understanding language, or swallowing safely. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T4#GNS324_U1_T4_h4)

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease treatment?

options.A: It relies entirely on expensive surgical interventions
options.B: It focuses on environmental conditions and empowerment rather than just fixing illness
options.C: It is handled exclusively by doctors in private clinics
options.D: It only applies to children and elderly populations

explanation: While disease treatment steps in after sickness occurs, health promotion looks at the bigger social and living conditions that keep people well in the first place. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the main difference between recruitment and selection?

options.A: Recruitment fires poor workers, while selection hires new replacements
options.B: Recruitment tests practical skills, while selection writes the job description
options.C: Recruitment is done only internally, while selection is done only externally
options.D: Recruitment attracts applicants, while selection chooses the best candidate

explanation: Easy way to remember: recruitment casts a wide net to get people to apply, while selection is the screening process where you pick the best person for the job. [learn more](GST321_U4_T1#GST321_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the most common nutritional shortage that causes microcytic anaemia?

options.A: Protein shortage
options.B: Vitamin C lack
options.C: Iron deficiency
options.D: Calcium deficiency

explanation: Great to know for clinicals! Without enough iron, the body cannot build proper hemoglobin, leaving red blood cells looking small and pale. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why is buying healthcare different from buying regular items like shoes or phones?

options.A: The price of medical care never changes based on economic factors
options.B: Patients can easily treat themselves without professional assistance
options.C: Healthcare items are always distributed by governments for free
options.D: People demand healthcare because they want health, not because it is a source of pleasure

explanation: Nobody wakes up wishing to visit the hospital for fun! We seek care simply to get our health back and function well. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of these topics calls for a qualitative design?

options.A: The effect of a specific dose of paracetamol on fever
options.B: The exact recovery time after an appendectomy
options.C: The daily emotional coping strategies of cancer survivors
options.D: The percentage of hospital staff who wash their hands

explanation: Brilliant! Exploring how someone feels and copes means listening to their personal story—classic qualitative territory. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of using lower individual drug doses in synergistic therapy?

options.A: It completely removes the need for nursing blood monitoring
options.B: It reduces the risk of toxic side effects for the patient
options.C: It allows patients to stop taking the drugs much sooner
options.D: It ensures the medication works instantly without absorption

explanation: Because the drugs boost each other, we can use smaller doses to get the job done, keeping the patient safer from harsh side effects. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a key nursing duty when giving a patient a new biological medication?

options.A: Ensuring the medication is stored in direct sunlight at room temperature
options.B: Crushing the vial contents into water for oral intake
options.C: Assuming all biological products are completely safe from side effects
options.D: Watching the patient closely for any signs of an allergic reaction

explanation: Because biological and animal-based drugs carry a higher risk of triggering the immune system, keeping a close eye on your patient is a must. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h8)

question: What vital sign must you watch most carefully after giving an IV opioid?

options.A: Oxygen saturation only
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Capillary refill
options.D: Body temperature

explanation: Safety first! Opioids can slow down the brain's breathing center, making your respiratory check the most important assessment in the room. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h7)

question: During a home visit, a nurse sees a parole patient acting paranoid, talking to unseen things, and throwing away meds. What is the nurse's priority?

options.A: Tell the patient's neighbors to handle the situation.
options.B: Report it to the care team right away to prevent a full relapse.
options.C: Wait three weeks until the next scheduled doctor visit.
options.D: Ignore it since the patient is living outside the hospital now.

explanation: Spot on! Paranoid behavior and tossing medications are urgent red flags. Acting fast helps the team step in before things escalate. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h7)

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out how much pain a patient is feeling?

options.A: Asking the patient and listening to them
options.B: Looking at the size of the injury
options.C: Watching for changes in resting pulse
options.D: Checking lab results for inflammation

explanation: Pain is personal! Only the patient truly knows what they are feeling, so their word is always our best guide. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h1)

question: If a patient just had surgery, which food category is most important to help close up that incision?

options.A: Energy-giving foods
options.B: Protective foods
options.C: Body-building foods
options.D: Perishable foods

explanation: You nailed it! Body-building foods are rich in proteins, which act like bricks and mortar to fix cut tissues and heal wounds. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T007#GNS227_U1_T007_h3)

question: When would a nurse use an oropharyngeal airway device?

options.A: In an unconscious patient lacking gag reflexes
options.B: To suction mucus from a patient's stomach
options.C: To deliver oral medications for high blood pressure
options.D: In a conscious patient who is talking normally

explanation: These airways can make an awake patient vomit. We only use them on deeply unconscious patients who won't gag on it. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h3)

question: An admission that is planned well in advance for a scheduled surgical procedure is called what?

options.A: An elective admission
options.B: An emergency admission
options.C: A transfer admission
options.D: An acute admission

explanation: Elective admissions are scheduled ahead of time because the patient's condition is stable enough to wait for a convenient date. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which requirement must be met before skilled home health nursing care can officially start?

options.A: The family must purchase a private hospital bed
options.B: The patient must win a local community award
options.C: A licensed physician must order the care
options.D: The nurse must live with the patient full-time

explanation: Home health services require a formal medical order from a doctor just like any other prescription or therapy. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h8)

question: Why is a 'return demonstration' the best way to see if a family caregiver knows how to do a dressing change?

options.A: It replaces the need to document anything in the patient chart.
options.B: It allows the nurse to leave the home early while the family works.
options.C: It ensures the family buys the most expensive medical supplies.
options.D: It proves they can physically perform the steps correctly rather than just nodding yes.

explanation: Seeing is believing! Having them do it in front of you ensures they really understand the steps, way better than just taking their word for it. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T4#GNS324_U3_T4_h6)

question: How does active listening help prevent sexual difficulties in a relationship?

options.A: It ensures that both partners always have identical sexual desires
options.B: It lets partners address needs and discomfort early before resentment builds
options.C: It replaces the need for medical evaluation of physical symptoms
options.D: It cures underlying chronic illnesses like diabetes and hypertension

explanation: Talking and listening openly allows couples to tackle physical or emotional hurdles together before they turn into major dysfunctions. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h5)

question: A nurse manager holds a staff meeting to ask everyone for ideas on how to fix the weekend scheduling roster. What leadership style is being used?

options.A: Coercive
options.B: Democratic
options.C: Laissez-faire
options.D: Autocratic

explanation: Asking the team for input and involving them in decisions is the hallmark of democratic leadership. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h5)

question: How does severe obesity negatively impact male reproductive health?

options.A: Obesity stops the pituitary gland from ever producing luteinizing hormone
options.B: Body fat physically blocks sperm from leaving the epididymis during ejaculation
options.C: Adipose cells directly attack mature sperm cells in the seminal fluid
options.D: Fat tissue converts extra testosterone into estrogen, disrupting the hormonal balance

explanation: Fatty tissue contains aromatase, an enzyme that turns testosterone into estrogen, which interferes with normal sperm creation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: Your patient just had shoulder surgery and is on bed rest. What is your next best move regarding AROM?

options.A: Encourage the patient to swing the arm rapidly to build strength quickly.
options.B: Check the medical orders and surgeon guidelines before allowing shoulder movement.
options.C: Ignore the surgery and start full arm rotations immediately.
options.D: Refuse to let the patient move any part of their entire body.

explanation: Always check the surgeon's rules first after an operation to make sure you protect the healing surgical site. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T2#GNS221_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the very first thing emergency responders do at an accident scene to protect a patient's spine?

options.A: Administering strong intravenous pain medication
options.B: Standing the patient up to test leg strength
options.C: Applying a rigid neck collar and securing the body
options.D: Massaging the neck muscles to relieve tension

explanation: That's correct! Putting on a stiff neck collar and securing the body keeps the spine still, preventing small fractures from turning into permanent paralysis. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T13#GNS222_U3_T13_h5)

question: A patient with an arterial line suddenly shows a drop in blood pressure on the monitor. What should you do first?

options.A: Give a large fluid bag without checking the patient
options.B: Just write it off as a machine error
options.C: Assess the patient and check if the line tubing is okay
options.D: Turn off the monitor computer to restart it

explanation: Never treat just the screen! Always validate monitor values by checking the patient first and making sure the equipment isn't kinked or disconnected. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason farmers use crop rotation in their fields?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any water source
options.B: Restoring soil fertility and breaking pest cycles
options.C: Ensuring that only one crop grows forever in a field
options.D: Increasing the retail price of vegetables

explanation: Rotating different crops is a smart farming trick. It gives the soil a break to regain nutrients and confuses pests so they don't take over! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h2)

question: How should a patient's palms face when they are in the standard anatomical position?

options.A: Facing forward
options.B: Facing backward
options.C: Facing each other
options.D: Facing upward

explanation: In the standard anatomical position, the arms rest at the sides with the palms turned forward and thumbs pointing outward. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which action using both hands is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among nurses?

options.A: Wiping skin with alcohol
options.B: Transporting safety boxes
options.C: Opening glass ampoules
options.D: Recapping used needles

explanation: Trying to guide a used needle back into its tiny cap with two hands is a classic hazard. That's why safety rules tell us never to recap used needles! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h2)

question: A manager promises extra pay for extra shifts, but staff know management never pays up. Which part of Vroom's theory is broken?

options.A: Hygiene factor
options.B: Expectancy
options.C: Instrumentality
options.D: Valence

explanation: You got it! Instrumentality is the link between doing a good job and actually getting the promised reward. If staff don't trust management, that link is broken. [learn more](GST321_U3_T5#GST321_U3_T5_h5)

question: A nurse wants to know the exact percentage of pregnant women at an antenatal clinic who sleep under treated mosquito nets. What type of question is this?

options.A: Descriptive
options.B: Causal
options.C: Relational
options.D: Interventional

explanation: You got this! Descriptive questions simply paint a picture of what is happening right now in a specific group of people. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h3)

question: Which symptom strongly points to an acute hemolytic transfusion reaction?

options.A: Lower back or flank pain
options.B: Gradual weight loss over days
options.C: Excessive daytime sleepiness
options.D: Severe localized skin dryness

explanation: When red cells break down inside the body, the kidneys take a hit, which often shows up as sharp lower back or flank pain. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h7)

question: Why do hospitals require independent double-checks for high-risk medications?

options.A: To ensure that two nurses share the blame if a patient is harmed
options.B: To provide a redundant barrier that catches individual calculation errors
options.C: To waste nursing time and slow down medication administration
options.D: To prove to hospital management that staffing levels are adequate

explanation: Two pairs of eyes are better than one! Having a colleague double-check a calculation creates a safety net to catch accidental errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GST319_U5_T8#GST319_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why do nurses appreciate capnography during patient sedation?

options.A: It stops skin breakdown on the fingers and toes
options.B: It shows how well the patient is breathing out carbon dioxide
options.C: It doesn't need batteries or power to work
options.D: It checks blood pressure much faster than a cuff

explanation: Capnography tracks breathing by measuring exhaled carbon dioxide, warning us if breathing slows down before oxygen levels even drop. Brilliant tool! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T2#GNS315_U4_T2_h3)

question: When is a nurse researcher most likely to use a non-directional hypothesis?

options.A: When there is strong evidence supporting an increase
options.B: When the statistical software requires a one-tailed test
options.C: When little previous research exists on the topic
options.D: When the null hypothesis has already been proven true

explanation: If no one has studied the topic much before, you might not know which way things will go, so you keep it non-directional. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should do when helping someone with a fresh thermal burn?

options.A: Apply antibiotic ointment to prevent infection
options.B: Apply ice packs directly to the wound to reduce swelling
options.C: Stop the burning process and apply cool water
options.D: Scrub the burn vigorously with antiseptic soap

explanation: Always stop the burning first and cool it with clean running water! Never use ice, though—it causes blood vessels to clamp down and makes the injury worse. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h4)

question: A patient wants an IUD right after an uncomplicated surgical abortion. What is the standard clinical practice?

options.A: She must wait for two normal menstrual periods
options.B: It can be safely inserted right away if there is no sign of infection
options.C: IUDs are never recommended after pregnancy termination
options.D: She must wait six weeks for her uterus to shrink

explanation: As long as there's no infection or trauma, an IUD can be placed immediately after the procedure. Saves the patient an extra trip! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T016#GNS226_U5_T016_h4)

question: What is an important preventive screening topic for women receiving long-term home health care?

options.A: Daily testing for adult growth hormone levels
options.B: Mammogram schedules and breast self-awareness
options.C: Monthly surgical checks for joint replacement
options.D: Weekly testing for acute kidney stone formation

explanation: Regular breast screenings and awareness are key components of preventive health maintenance for adult women. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T13#GNS324_U3_T13_h7)

question: What is the primary danger associated with polypharmacy in older patients?

options.A: Complete elimination of side effects from strong painkillers
options.B: A high likelihood of adverse drug reactions and harmful interactions
options.C: Rapid improvement in cognitive processing speed and memory
options.D: Immediate cure of all existing chronic and acute health conditions

explanation: Taking many different medicines at once greatly increases the chance that they will interact badly with each other or cause harmful side effects. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h6)

question: Which type of nerve pathway carries messages from the body up to the brain and spinal cord?

options.A: Efferent pathway
options.B: Afferent pathway
options.C: Autonomic pathway
options.D: Motor pathway

explanation: Spot on! Remember: 'A'fferent arrives at the central nervous system with sensory info from your body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What acts as the roadmap for a meeting, listing the topics and time frames?

options.A: The strategic plan
options.B: The meeting agenda
options.C: The attendance register
options.D: The financial ledger

explanation: An agenda keeps everyone focused by outlining what will be discussed and for how long. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h3)

question: What is the first emergency medicine to give if a newborn's heart rate stays under 60 despite breathing support and chest compressions?

options.A: Naloxone
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Epinephrine

explanation: Epinephrine is our go-to emergency drug to help jumpstart the heart rate and improve heart muscle squeeze during severe bradycardia. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h6)

question: What is the function of the one-way valves inside medium veins?

options.A: Filter bacteria out of returning blood
options.B: Add oxygen back into venous blood
options.C: Regulate body temperature in limbs
options.D: Prevent blood from flowing backward

explanation: Venous valves ensure that blood moves in only one direction—toward the heart—against the pull of gravity. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why do nurses prefer IV medications over oral tablets during severe emergencies?

options.A: It is completely painless for the patient
options.B: It delivers medication directly into the bloodstream for fast action
options.C: Oral medications are illegal in hospital emergency units
options.D: It eliminates the need for any dosage calculations

explanation: IV meds skip the digestive system completely, hitting the bloodstream instantly when every single second counts. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T7#GNS112_U7_T7_h6)

question: Which of these blood-borne viruses is famously tough and can survive for days on environmental surfaces?

options.A: Malaria parasite
options.B: Tuberculosis bacterium
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Hepatitis B Virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is remarkably hardy outside the body compared to many other viruses, staying infectious for a surprisingly long time. Good thing we practice strict infection control! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h3)

question: When prioritizing health issues in a community, what does 'magnitude' mean?

options.A: The distance from the village to the nearest hospital
options.B: The number of people affected by the health problem
options.C: The total financial cost of medical treatment
options.D: The physical size of the local health clinic

explanation: Exactly right! Magnitude simply tells you how widespread the issue is—how many community members are actually dealing with it. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h4)

question: How do Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs) mostly stop stomach acid?

options.A: Neutralizing existing acid directly inside the stomach lumen
options.B: Blocking the hydrogen-potassium enzyme pump in parietal cells
options.C: Coating the ulcer base with a thick protective physical paste
options.D: Killing the bacteria responsible for stomach lining infections

explanation: PPIs target the exact tiny pumps in the stomach lining that push acid out. Turn off the pump, and acid production slows right down! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which part of the blastocyst eventually grows into the actual fetus?

options.A: The outer trophoblast
options.B: The blastocoele fluid
options.C: The inner cell mass
options.D: The zona pellucida

explanation: Spot on! The inner cell mass contains the special cells that will form the tissues of the baby itself. Keep up the great work! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h2)

question: A pregnant woman complains of terrible night heartburn. What easy adjustment can the nurse suggest for bedtime?

options.A: Elevate the head of the bed by several inches
options.B: Sleep lying flat on her right side with no pillows
options.C: Sleep flat on her stomach with a pillow under her hips
options.D: Use extra heavy blankets to keep the abdomen warm

explanation: Propping up the head of the bed uses gravity to keep stomach acid where it belongs while she sleeps. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h5)

question: What is the main job of the cerebrospinal fluid that surrounds the brain?

options.A: To cool down the brain during high fevers
options.B: To supply all oxygen needed by neurons
options.C: To generate electrical impulses for thinking
options.D: To cushion the brain and provide buoyancy

explanation: Cerebrospinal fluid acts like a water cushion, protecting the brain from bumps and making it feel lighter inside the skull. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why do we usually draw blood cultures from two different sites?

options.A: To reduce the pain experienced in one single arm
options.B: To help distinguish true infection from skin contamination
options.C: To speed up the laboratory processing time significantly
options.D: To collect a larger total volume of blood for testing

explanation: Drawing from two spots helps us know if bacteria in the bottle came from the patient's bloodstream or just from the skin during the poke. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which of the following should you NOT tell a patient who is monitoring their blood pressure at home?

options.A: Keep a written log of all blood pressure and pulse readings
options.B: Ensure the arm is supported comfortably at heart level
options.C: Stop taking prescribed medications whenever readings look normal
options.D: Rest quietly for five minutes before taking a measurement

explanation: Never let a patient stop their meds just because their numbers look good today—the medicine is likely why the numbers look good! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h9)

question: How should you support a joint while doing passive range of motion exercises?

options.A: Placing your hands above and below the joint
options.B: Letting the limb dangle freely without support
options.C: Holding the joint tightly right at its center point
options.D: Pulling firmly on the fingers or toes

explanation: Great job! Cradling the joint with hands positioned above and below gives solid support and protects the surrounding tissue. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T3#GNS221_U1_T3_h4)

question: If the local currency drops in value, making imported drugs much more expensive, what should the DRF committee do?

options.A: Keep selling remaining stock at old prices until everything is completely gone
options.B: Borrow money from patients to pay for the next batch of imported drugs
options.C: Adjust selling prices based on current replacement costs to protect the fund
options.D: Stop selling medications entirely and wait for inflation to reverse itself naturally

explanation: If you don't adjust prices during currency drops, your sales revenue won't be enough to buy the next batch of drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T4#GNS215_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which injection is routinely given to every newborn baby to prevent dangerous bleeding?

options.A: Vitamin K
options.B: Iron drops
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Folic acid

explanation: Newborns have little tummies that haven't built up clotting factors yet. Giving Vitamin K right after birth protects them against bleeding disorders. Excellent clinical knowledge to carry into the ward! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h5)

question: What is the difference between anonymity and confidentiality?

options.A: Anonymity means no one can link data to a name; confidentiality keeps known identities secret
options.B: Anonymity is optional in nursing research; confidentiality is strictly mandatory
options.C: Anonymity applies only to secondary data; confidentiality applies to primary data
options.D: There is no difference between the two terms in clinical research studies

explanation: Anonymity means nobody (not even the researcher) knows whose data is whose. Confidentiality means you know who they are, but you keep their identity locked away safe. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of using hydrotherapy (water exercise) in rehab?

options.A: Water buoyancy reduces joint stress during physical exercise.
options.B: It replaces the need for any nutritional support.
options.C: It eliminates all risks of secondary skin infections.
options.D: It completely cures chronic neurological disorders in days.

explanation: Well done! The water helps support the patient's weight, taking pressure off painful or weak joints so they can move more easily. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h5)

question: Why does parental apathy pose a serious problem for the PTA?

options.A: It forces the government to close down all private hospitals
options.B: It automatically increases the academic salaries of teachers
options.C: It leads to poor attendance and lack of support for school programs
options.D: It stops students from participating in sports competitions

explanation: When parents show little interest in meetings, collective decision-making and community-driven projects fail to take off. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T5#GNS225_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is it smart for a nurse to involve religious leaders and local heads in a community health plan?

options.A: To dispense prescription antibiotics to villagers
options.B: To gain community buy-in and policy support
options.C: To diagnose complex medical surgical conditions
options.D: To audit hospital financial expenditure records

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders have great influence over the people, so having their backing helps the community welcome new health programs. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T3#GNS124_U5_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of a dangerous, severe allergic reaction to contrast dye?

options.A: Widespread itchy hives on the skin
options.B: Mild metallic taste in the mouth
options.C: Sudden difficulty in breathing
options.D: Swelling of the lips and tongue

explanation: A metallic taste is totally normal! Hives, swollen lips, and trouble breathing, however, are red flags that mean we need to act fast. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T16#GNS221_U2_T16_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge in community mobilisation?

options.A: Cultural resistance to new health ideas
options.B: Political interference from local figures
options.C: Guaranteed 100% funding and instant community obedience
options.D: Apathy and lack of initial interest from residents

explanation: Communities are rarely instantly obedient or fully funded; engagement is usually hard work filled with resistance and roadblocks. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the most effective way at the community level to stop the spread of paragonimiasis?

options.A: Treating entire river water sources with heavy industrial chlorine
options.B: Banning the commercial sale of all freshwater fish species
options.C: Immunizing all school-aged children with a parasite vaccine
options.D: Educating the public to cook freshwater crabs thoroughly

explanation: Spot on! Health education is key. Teaching people to cook their crabs thoroughly stops the parasite right in its tracks. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T26#GNS313_U2_T26_h8)

question: How do cross-sectional study findings help Nigerian nurse managers in clinical practice?

options.A: By proving which nurse caused specific patient readmissions
options.B: By eliminating the need for daily nursing shift handovers
options.C: By guaranteeing permanent funding from international donor agencies
options.D: By providing local data to improve resource allocation and healthcare planning

explanation: Local data helps managers see real community needs clearly, making it easier to send staff and supplies right where they are needed most. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h9)

question: Which of these actions is an example of professional negligence?

options.A: Reporting a faulty infusion pump to the biomedical engineering department
options.B: Asking a patient to explain their understanding of a surgical procedure
options.C: Failing to check a patient blood pressure before giving a blood pressure medication
options.D: Refusing to participate in an unethical research study on patients

explanation: Great job! Giving a blood pressure medication without checking if their BP is already too low is a dangerous slip in the standard of care. [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h5)

question: A nurse wants to understand why mothers in a village refuse to bring children for immunization. Which method is most suitable?

options.A: Focus group discussion with mothers
options.B: Checking the expiration dates of vaccine vials
options.C: Measuring the mid-upper arm circumference of infants
options.D: Counting the number of houses in the ward

explanation: Group discussions allow community members to freely share cultural beliefs, fears, and reasons behind specific health behaviors. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is allowed on a full fluid diet, but NOT on a clear fluid diet?

options.A: Plain water
options.B: Transparent beef broth
options.C: Clear apple juice
options.D: Plain milk

explanation: Clear fluids you can see straight through (like water or broth). Full fluids include cloudy items like milk and custard! [learn more](GNS227_U6_T001#GNS227_U6_T001_h3)

question: Why is it so important to involve local community members when planning a health program?

options.A: It ensures cultural acceptance and long-term program sustainability
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional nursing staff entirely
options.C: It guarantees immediate federal funding for hospital construction
options.D: It prevents any future outbreaks of infectious diseases

explanation: Brilliant! When a community helps design their own health programs, they take ownership of them, and the project lasts much longer because it respects their local culture. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T9#GNS225_U1_T9_h5)

question: What do we mean by clinical variation in healthcare?

options.A: Changes in the weather that affect hospital air conditioning
options.B: The total financial budget allocated to the maternity ward
options.C: The exact number of patients admitted to the hospital daily
options.D: Differences in how tasks are performed or outcomes achieved

explanation: Variation simply refers to the differences in practices or results across different staff members or shifts. Standardizing care helps reduce this! [learn more](GST319_U2_T6#GST319_U2_T6_h4)

question: Which chromosomal change causes Down syndrome?

options.A: Trisomy 13
options.B: Trisomy 21
options.C: Deletion of chromosome 5
options.D: Monosomy X

explanation: Down syndrome is caused by the presence of an extra third copy of chromosome 21. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h6)

question: Why is continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) often chosen over standard hemodialysis for critically ill patients?

options.A: It can be performed easily without any specialized equipment
options.B: It does not require any form of vascular access in the body
options.C: It completely cures chronic kidney disease within a few days
options.D: It removes fluids and toxins much more slowly and gently

explanation: CRRT filters blood continuously over 24 hours, making it much safer for hemodynamically unstable patients in the ICU. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h7)

question: How do penicillins primarily kill bacteria?

options.A: Disrupting normal metabolic folate pathways
options.B: Binding directly to human liver enzymes
options.C: Blocking essential nucleic acid replication
options.D: Inhibiting bacterial cell wall synthesis

explanation: Spot on! Penicillins mess up the building blocks of the bacterial cell wall. Without a strong wall, the bacteria burst open and die. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h2)

question: A patient scheduled for MVA is visibly shaking and expresses fear of severe pain. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Sit close, explain the steps calmly, and offer emotional reassurance
options.B: Cancel the procedure immediately and reschedule for another day
options.C: Tell her that pain is minor and she should try to stay strong
options.D: Administer a strong general anesthetic drug without a doctor's order

explanation: Anxious patients benefit greatly from calm explanations, validation of their feelings, and reassurance, which helps reduce physical tension and perceived pain. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h4)

question: What is the main job of the internal male reproductive organs altogether?

options.A: To control secondary sex characteristics only
options.B: To filter waste products from the blood
options.C: To regulate body temperature in the groin
options.D: To produce, nourish, and transport sperm

explanation: These internal organs work like a well-oiled factory team to manufacture sperm, mix in helpful protective fluids, and deliver everything smoothly. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthcare teamwork?

options.A: Heavy staff workloads leading to severe burnout
options.B: Open daily communication between departments
options.C: Professional silos where workers isolate themselves
options.D: Rigid and intimidating workplace hierarchies

explanation: Spot on! Open communication helps teamwork thrive. Burnout, silos, and strict hierarchies are the real walls that block good collaboration. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h6)

question: How are wearable health trackers beginning to influence professional health records?

options.A: By replacing the need for licensed nurses in hospital wards
options.B: By serving as the primary billing invoice for insurance companies
options.C: By feeding real-time patient metrics directly into clinical systems
options.D: By automatically prescribing medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Wearables like smartwatches are starting to integrate live patient data such as heart rate and activity into medical records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is entomology?

options.A: The study of parasitic worms and flukes
options.B: The analysis of fungal infections
options.C: The scientific study of insects
options.D: The clinical study of human blood cells

explanation: Entomology is specifically the branch of zoology that focuses on insects and their relationship with the environment and humans. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why is the agricultural sector so important when health workers try to improve nutrition?

options.A: Because farming practices have no impact on community health outcomes
options.B: Because farmers are legally required to diagnose nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Because agricultural workers manage all rural health clinics
options.D: Because agriculture determines how much and what types of food are produced

explanation: Brilliant! Farming dictates what food is available and how varied the food supply is, making agriculture the very foundation of good nutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of social services in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Performing major orthopedic surgeries in the operating theatre
options.B: Addressing non-medical social and economic challenges affecting health
options.C: Conducting laboratory blood tests and urinalysis
options.D: Prescribing strong antibiotics for bacterial infections

explanation: Good health isn't just about medicine! Social services look at things like poverty, living conditions, and family support that affect how well a patient recovers. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T2#GNS112_U2_T2_h5)

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: The onset of convulsive seizures
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h3)

question: What is the basic functional unit of the kidney called?

options.A: Neuron
options.B: Lobule
options.C: Alveolus
options.D: Nephron

explanation: Each kidney contains over a million nephrons, which are responsible for filtering blood and forming urine. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a pathway for lymphatic drainage from the uterus and ovaries?

options.A: Axillary lymph nodes
options.B: External iliac nodes
options.C: Internal iliac nodes
options.D: Lumbar lymph nodes

explanation: Axillary nodes drain the arms and breasts, not the deep pelvic reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h6)

question: As a general nurse working at Tier 3, which of these is your best intervention?

options.A: Performing electroconvulsive therapy
options.B: Prescribing complex antipsychotic drug cocktails
options.C: Performing neurosurgery for trauma
options.D: Delivering basic psychological first aid and supportive counseling

explanation: Spot on! Nurses at Tier 3 provide wonderful, comforting care like active listening and psychological first aid without needing a psychiatry degree. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h4)

question: What does having an 'appreciation for a system' mean in a busy hospital setting?

options.A: Ensuring every single department makes a profit
options.B: Keeping hospital departments strictly separated so no one gets distracted
options.C: Recognizing how different departments depend on each other to reach a common goal
options.D: Giving regular awards to hardworking nursing staff

explanation: Think of a hospital like a football team—pharmacy, lab, and nursing all have to pass the ball to each other to win for the patient! [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main goal of disease prevention in public health?

options.A: Finding new surgical methods for complex chronic illnesses
options.B: Stopping health problems before they start or halting their progress
options.C: Reducing the cost of pharmaceutical manufacturing plants
options.D: Increasing hospital admission rates for routine checkups

explanation: You've got this! Prevention is all about stopping illness proactively before it takes hold, rather than just treating symptoms later. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h1)

question: Which bone shape category does the patella ( kneecap) belong to?

options.A: Flat bone
options.B: Irregular bone
options.C: Long bone
options.D: Sesamoid bone

explanation: Sesamoid bones like the patella develop inside tendons to protect them from excessive wear and tear. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention?

options.A: Running a stress-reduction workshop for healthy adults
options.B: Screening high school students for early signs of depression
options.C: Administering emergency life support for a drug overdose
options.D: Providing long-term rehabilitation for chronic schizophrenia

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt treatment to stop mild symptoms from becoming severe disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a job of the ordinary sweat glands (eccrine glands)?

options.A: Excreting tiny amounts of body waste
options.B: Producing thick, smelly sweat in the armpits
options.C: Helping cool down the body through sweat evaporation
options.D: Releasing watery fluid onto the skin

explanation: Spot on! Armpit and groin sweat comes from apocrine glands, while your ordinary (eccrine) glands make watery sweat all over to keep you cool. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's bedside locker to clear out old, forgotten food brought by family?

question: What is the main purpose of herd immunity in a community?

question: Which of the following is an example of an assistive technology used for learning disabilities?

question: Why do healthcare workers usually resist new changes in the workplace?

question: How should a nurse properly document physical examination findings?

question: What causes platelets to stick together and form a temporary plug at an injury site?

question: Why should you always share your assessment findings back with the community members who helped you?

options.C: Community clinics handle complex surgeries daily
options.D: Nurses are usually the first health workers patients see with early symptoms

explanation: Spotting early signs at the grass-roots level means we can refer patients quickly and save lives. Great nursing starts in the community! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h1)

question: During a hospital admission assessment, what is a vital detail to find out about a patient's substance history?

options.A: The date and time of their last dose
options.B: How much money they spend each month
options.C: The name of the friend who introduced them
options.D: Their personal opinion on local drug laws

explanation: You're doing great! Knowing when they last used helps you predict and prepare for any withdrawal symptoms that might pop up during their stay. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is your absolute first priority when checking a patient who might have asphyxia?

options.A: Checking skin integrity over pressure points
options.B: Reviewing past medical and family history
options.C: Checking airway, breathing, and circulation
options.D: Measuring exact daily fluid intake and output

explanation: ABC comes first in every single emergency! Securing life-sustaining functions is always your top duty. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T8#GNS123_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse during the implementation phase?

options.A: Taking over all physical labor so locals do not work
options.B: Writing laws to force people to attend health clinics
options.C: Sitting in an office away from the project site
options.D: Providing technical guidance and supporting community action

explanation: Nurses act as facilitators and technical guides while the community executes the planned health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h7)

question: What treatment involves placing tiny radioactive sources directly inside or close to a cervical tumor?

options.A: Hysterectomy
options.B: Cryotherapy
options.C: Brachytherapy
options.D: Chemotherapy

explanation: You've got it! 'Brachy' means close—so brachytherapy places radiation right next to or inside the tumor to target bad cells while sparing healthy tissue. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h6)

question: Which skin receptors are primarily responsible for detecting light touch?

options.A: Meissner's corpuscles
options.B: Pacinian corpuscles
options.C: Sweat glands
options.D: Arrector pili muscles

explanation: Meissner's corpuscles are specialized nerve endings located close to the skin surface that sense light touch. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is needed to keep safety improvements working over the long haul?

options.A: Introducing new policies and never checking them
options.B: Continuous education, audits, and feedback loops
options.C: Relying solely on the memory of senior nurses
options.D: Punishing staff members who forget safety rules

explanation: Safety isn't a one-time event! It takes ongoing training, regular check-ins (audits), and sharing data with the team to make good habits stick. [learn more](GST319_U6_T6#GST319_U6_T6_h7)

question: How does proper financial control directly help patient care?

options.A: It completely removes the need for doctors to write prescriptions
options.B: It allows nurses to spend less time documenting patient symptoms
options.C: It guarantees that patients never have to wait in the emergency room
options.D: It ensures necessary equipment and medications are available when needed

explanation: When money is managed well, your ward will steadily have the tools, drugs, and supplies required to treat patients safely. [learn more](GST321_U1_T23#GST321_U1_T23_h2)
